president--apm.title: Reset Nigeria
president--apm.note: Unveiled in Abuja. No full text has been published online that we could find.

pledges.text: Lower the cost of living and the cost of production so Nigerian businesses can compete.
Let manufacturers connect to the national grid for electricity cheaper than diesel generators.
Pursue macroeconomic stability for growth, jobs, higher incomes and lower living costs.
Tie each promise to a responsible institution, a delivery plan and measurable results, reviewed at 100 days and over three years.
Serve one transitional four-year term to reset the political system.
Keep national development plans running whichever party holds power.

president--sdp.title: Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity: Governance and Accelerated Development, Blueprint of a New Nigeria 2027–2031
president--sdp.note: Unveiled in Abuja. Not published online; supporters say copies are available on request by email.

pledges.text: Bring petrol to ₦200 per litre within the first year by expanding domestic refining and changing crude supply to local refineries.
Act against terrorism, kidnapping and illegal mining, and reclaim territory held by terrorists.
Free healthcare, including free medical screening twice a year.
Free education as part of a social welfare programme.
Policies to cut transport and housing costs.
Expand farming in year one, then irrigation, food storage and processing.
Industrial clusters plus rail, broadband, housing and water projects in years two and three.
Base budgets on Chapter II of the Constitution, create a Presidential Delivery Office in the first 100 days and publish a performance dashboard.

president--ndc.note: Set out an agenda at his campaign launch on 21 August 2026. As of 4 November, critics said no written manifesto had been published.

pledges.text: Move the economy from consumption to production and cut dependence on imports.
Better intelligence and coordination between security agencies, stronger policing and border control, and community early-warning systems.
Support farming with security, irrigation, rural roads, storage, finance and agro-processing.
Strengthen basic education, universities, and technical and vocational training.
Improve maternal and child health, essential medicines and support for health workers.
Tie public spending to defined objectives and measurable outcomes.

president--adc.note: We haven't found a published 2027 manifesto. These are pledges reported from campaign rallies.

pledges.text: Restore the fuel subsidy.
Improve security.
Create jobs.

president--apc.title: From Reforms to Prosperity
president--apc.note: Unveiled by President Bola Tinubu at the APC presidential rally in Port Harcourt on 7 November 2026. The 109-page document is dated 28 October 2026. It groups the Renewed Hope agenda into four pillars: a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. It says every commitment will carry a baseline, target, cost, owner and reporting date on a public delivery tracker. A copy was published online by Proshare.

pledges.text: Safer lives and communities: stronger protection against terrorism, banditry and kidnapping, a police service that responds when needed, and better protection of Nigeria's borders.

Recruit, train and deploy 28,000 additional Army personnel and 50,000 new police officers, moving towards one police officer for every 400 people, with public reporting; cover all mapped borders with electronic surveillance and all identified mining sites with Mining Marshals.
Bring inflation down to single digits, at most 8% year-on-year by the end of 2031, subject to credible, independent monetary policy.
Expand social protection to 20 million verified people by 2030, with school feeding nationwide, and enforce the ₦70,000 minimum wage in every state.
Reach half of all economically active Nigerians with equitable consumer credit by 2030.
Lift annual non-oil exports to at least $15 billion by 2031, including $1 billion from processed cocoa butter, and raise manufacturing to at least 12% of GDP.
Reach at least 7,500MW sustained average and 10,000MW peak power generation by 2031, cut power losses and uncollected bills to at most 16%, and install seven million more meters.
Create one million export-linked jobs for young Nigerians through talent and services exports by 2030, and halve youth unemployment by 2031.
Skill two million young people and make 30 million Nigerians digitally literate.
Expand domestic food production, storage and processing, halve the food lost after harvest, and move goods faster and cheaper between states.
Halve the number of out-of-school children, increase the number completing school, and deploy 20,000 additional teachers.
Expand health insurance from more than 23 million enrollees to 40% of Nigerians, and raise functioning primary health centres from 53% to at least 90%.
Deliver 154,800 housing units under the Tinubu Mass Social Housing Scheme, working towards 200,000 homes, tracked on a public dashboard.
Expand the national fibre backbone to at least 125,000km and port cargo to at least 180 million tonnes a year.

Extend digital case management from the superior courts to magistrate courts by 2029, and publish allocations for every one of the 774 local councils with clear performance and accountability standards.
Launch a Citizen Service Guarantee with published service standards and response times, and hold quarterly citizen engagements with published outcomes.
In the first 100 days, publish baselines and named owners for every headline commitment, the first quarterly cost-of-living basket, and an independent audit of unfinished or underused public assets.

gov--lagos--apc.title: The Lagos Promise (100 pledges)
gov--lagos--apc.note: Unveiled at the Wole Soyinka Centre, Iganmu. The campaign says 87 pledges are within state powers and 13 depend on the federal government or others.

pledges.text: Raise maternal and child centres from 6 to 15, build general hospitals at Ogombo and Ibeju-Lekki, and upgrade 100 primary health centres.
Within 100 days, a bill for a Child Protection and Nutrition Agency so every child under 18 is in school or learning a trade.
Place technical-school students with employers for 6 to 12 months, with the state paying 40% of their stipend.
Extend the Blue Line to Okokomaiko, link the Blue and Red lines at National Theatre, and work with the federal government on the Green Line.
Mortgages with a 10% deposit.
A state wealth fund with an independent board that publishes its accounts.
Service charters: complaints acknowledged in 48 hours and resolved within 30 days.

gov--lagos--ndc.title: Ònà Tuntun (New Road), 34 commitments
gov--lagos--ndc.note: Unveiled in Lagos in late October 2026.

pledges.text: Deliver 150,000 homes in four years.
Free healthcare for pregnant women and children under 16.
Free education through secondary and technical college, free textbooks, school meals, and free transport for pupils in uniform.
Better connect the Red and Blue rail lines, and move road maintenance to local governments.
Review major public-private partnerships and publish an independent review of former governors' benefits.

gov--akwa-ibom--adc.title: Eight-point manifesto
gov--akwa-ibom--adc.note: Announced at a press briefing in Uyo.

pledges.text: A 'fourth tier' of government in the state's 2,664 villages, with a monthly allowance for village needs.
Extension services, mechanisation, inputs, storage and market access; support for fishermen and rice farmers in Ini.
Modernise local government secretariats with 1.5km access roads to each.
Housing and car loans for government workers.
Education support for up to four children of each state worker, from nursery to university.

gov--oyo--apc.title: Oyo AHEAD
gov--oyo--apc.note: A seven-pillar blueprint unveiled in Ibadan.

pledges.text: Local government autonomy from his first day in office.
Raise the state's internally generated revenue to ₦150 billion without new burdens on residents and businesses.
A youth fund starting with ₦10 billion.
Finish ongoing roads, with a 20-year warranty on every new road.
Free health insurance for infants, pregnant women and over-70s, raising enrolment from 271,000 to 500,000 in two years; general hospitals in the six LGAs without one.
Class sizes of 30, and skills centres in every zone.
Insurance for 10,000 farmers and a produce board through an Oyo Export Council.
A state electricity regulator and replacement of faulty transformers every six months.

gov--oyo--apm.title: Omituntun 3.0: Continuity, Competence and Community
gov--oyo--apm.note: An abridged manifesto is on the campaign website; the campaign says the full version is coming. The launch report lists no specific pledges.

gov--kwara--pdp.note: The campaign says its manifesto, 'My Covenant with Kwara', will be unveiled in Ilorin on 12 November 2026.

gov--kaduna--prp.note: We haven't found a published manifesto. These are pledges from his campaign vision statement.

pledges.text: Closer work between security agencies and communities, and economic opportunities to reduce the causes of conflict.
Better school buildings and teacher training, wider access in rural areas, and curricula matched to jobs.
Revive primary health centres and strengthen maternal and child health in underserved areas.
Better access to fertiliser and other inputs, and youth jobs in farming.

gov--rivers--adp.note: We haven't found a published manifesto. This pledge is from a campaign statement.

pledges.text: Create 500,000 direct and indirect jobs and empowerment opportunities in the first 365 days.

gov--benue--pdp.note: We haven't found a published manifesto. These are pledges reported from his campaign.

pledges.text: Make security the top priority, and repair rural roads and bridges that slow security response.
A ₦2 billion interest-free revolving student loan scheme, prioritising young people from areas hit by insecurity.
Let local governments manage their own statutory funds, and cut leakages and unnecessary spending.
Allow ranching businesses that comply with state and federal land, environment and quarantine laws.

gov--niger--pdp.title: 10-point development agenda
gov--niger--pdp.note: The launch report names the agenda's areas but not all ten points, and gives no figures.

pledges.text: Act decisively against banditry and kidnapping.
Strengthen agriculture.
Improve water supply.
Improve healthcare, and pensioners' welfare.

ADC.title: ADC and New Framework of Electoral Campaign
ADC.note: Adopted at the party's national convention. No full text published online that we could find.

pledges.text: Move from an oil-dependent, consumption-driven economy to production, through regional value chains in farming, manufacturing, logistics and technology.
A living wage, agreed between government, employers and labour.
Declare a state of emergency in education.
Prioritise preventive healthcare.
Coordinate intelligence by law and decentralise policing under national standards.
An electoral commission free from executive control, and performance audits of ADC governments.
